teaser_figure.message: No teaser image API key configured. Prompt was written to disk. Prompt was also copied to the clipboard. Paste it into the Gemini web app to generate the teaser figure manually.
teaser_figure.prompt: Create a single polished teaser figure for an ML paper review summary. The output should read like a presentation-quality overview graphic, not a raw markdown rendering. Use the extracted report content below as authoritative content to place into the figure. Preserve factual wording, numeric values, and status labels from the source. Treat the following layout/style instructions as fixed constraints derived from the reference demos/compgcn/teaser_reference.png. Treat the attached reference image as a hard layout-and-style target, not as loose inspiration. If any conflict appears between content length and layout fidelity, preserve layout fidelity first and shrink or wrap text. Keep colors unchanged and keep the relative positions of all modules unchanged; only adjust module width/height slightly based on content length. All text should use Times New Roman. There is no strict text-length limit inside each module; automatically adjust font sizes, line breaks, spacing, and box sizes for the most visually balanced result. Do not invent any extra claims, metrics, or statuses. The Summary module is mandatory and must be visible on the right side with both Strengths and Weaknesses content. The Technical Positioning figure must reuse the provided technical reference image, not a substituted architecture image. Use final_review content as canonical source text and preserve wording exactly; do not paraphrase, merge, or drop any required module content. [Fixed Layout Instructions] - Keep the overall teaser layout structure and relative module positions consistent with the reference design. - The top-right area contains status badges; preserve their relative placement and badge style. - All status badges use rounded-rectangle backgrounds. - The lower row includes Improvement and Reduction badges; preserve their relative placement. - The right-side summary panel keeps Strengths above Weaknesses, with the specified bottom background colors. - Claim rows should be laid out adaptively based on content, with no fixed per-line text limit. [Template Geometry] Lock these structural regions to the template's geometry: - title_banner: bbox=(0.040,0.040)-(0.970,0.150). Restore the dark top banner spanning nearly the full width, with the title left-aligned inside it, followed by the summary text — do not prefix the summary with 'TL;DR' or any other label. - task_badge: bbox=(0.750,0.040)-(0.980,0.100). Place the task label as a rounded badge right-aligned at the top-right corner, directly above the status badge row. Its width must auto-fit the text content — do not fix or extend the left edge to fill the full bbox width. Right edge stays pinned at the right margin; only the left edge floats with content length. - status_badges: bbox=(0.670,0.080)-(0.980,0.145). Preserve the top-right status badge strip as a tight horizontal run of rounded badges with the original ordering and spacing. - delta_badges: bbox=(0.770,0.120)-(0.980,0.175). Keep the Improvement and Reduction badges on their own lower row directly beneath the status badges. - main_canvas: bbox=(0.040,0.150)-(0.970,0.920). Preserve the large light-gray body shell under the header; do not switch to a flat white or fully reflowed canvas. - technical_panel: bbox=(0.050,0.170)-(0.560,0.560). Keep the technical-positioning block on the left side of the body, occupying the largest panel width. - claims_panel: bbox=(0.560,0.170)-(0.800,0.560). Keep the claim/evidence rows in the middle-right column rather than moving them below the figure or into the summary panel. - summary_panel: bbox=(0.800,0.170)-(0.960,0.920). Keep the summary column docked on the far right with stacked Strengths and Weaknesses blocks. - strengths_panel: bbox=(0.800,0.580)-(0.960,0.750). Restore the green-tinted Strengths background in the upper part of the right summary column. - weaknesses_panel: bbox=(0.800,0.750)-(0.960,0.920). Restore the pink-tinted Weaknesses background in the lower part of the right summary column. - experiments_panel: bbox=(0.050,0.580)-(0.790,0.900). Keep the experiment/result tables across the lower-left and lower-middle area, below the technical and claims panels. [Template Visual Anchors] Reference template image: demos\compgcn\teaser_reference.png; rely on the attached template image and fixed module constraints. [Fixed Badge Styles] - Task: text color RGB(30,40,80); rounded-rectangle background RGB(235,238,248); right-aligned directly above the status badge row; width auto-fits content (do not stretch to full row width). - Supported: text color RGB(88,144,78); left icon is a check mark with RGB(0,150,100); rounded-rectangle background RGB(172,215,142). - Partially supported / Inconclusive (top-right area only — do NOT use this combined label in claims rows): text color RGB(182,140,2); left icon is a triangular warning symbol (⚠) — do NOT use a circle, question mark, or any other icon; the triangle border is RGB(184,134,11) with a white internal exclamation mark; rounded-rectangle background RGB(254,230,149). - Partially supported (claims row badge): text color RGB(182,140,2); left icon is a triangular warning symbol (⚠) — same icon as above; rounded-rectangle background RGB(254,230,149). Label reads '⚠ Partially supported'. - Inconclusive (claims row badge): text color RGB(182,140,2); left icon is a triangular warning symbol (⚠) — same icon as above; rounded-rectangle background RGB(254,230,149). Label reads '⚠ Inconclusive'. - In conflict: text color RGB(200,29,49); left icon is an X with RGB(139,0,0); rounded-rectangle background RGB(239,148,158). - Improvement: text color RGB(86,133,44); rounded-rectangle background RGB(117,189,66). - Reduction: text color RGB(133,19,44); rounded-rectangle background RGB(229,76,94). [Fixed Content Rules] - The task label badge must always appear right-aligned directly above the status badge row, using fixed colors (background RGB(235,238,248), text RGB(30,40,80)); its width auto-fits the text content — do not fix the left edge or stretch the badge to fill the row width; its text is extracted from the 'Task' field in [Report Content]. - The top-right status badge area must always show exactly three fixed badges in this order: '✓ Supported', '⚠ Partially supported / Inconclusive', '✗ In conflict'. These are fixed template elements; do not derive, replace, or omit any of them based on claim row statuses or execution results. The second badge must literally read '⚠ Partially supported / Inconclusive' with a triangular ⚠ icon. All three badges are right-aligned as a compact horizontal group; Supported shifts right accordingly. - The Improvement and Reduction badges must always appear below the status badges with fixed labels ('Improvement', 'Reduction'), fixed colors, and fixed positions — do not modify their text or derive them from execution results. - The claims section should show exactly 3 claim rows, and they must be dynamically extracted from the report's claims table using the Claim, Evidence, and Status information. - In claims rows, each claim's status badge must display the exact status label from the claim's Status field (e.g., '⚠ Inconclusive', '⚠ Partially supported', '✓ Supported', '✗ In conflict') — do NOT substitute the combined top-right badge label '⚠ Partially supported / Inconclusive' for individual claim row badges. - In the claims module, each claim sentence must be visually bold in the figure. - Each claim row has no fixed text-length requirement; wrap and resize based on content for the cleanest layout. - The technical positioning module must directly use the extracted figure/image reference and table content. - The technical positioning visual must reuse the provided technical reference image faithfully (same subject/structure). - The experiment module must directly use the extracted main-result and ablation tables below. - For the Strengths section, use bottom background color RGB(200,229,179). - For the Weaknesses section, use bottom background color RGB(245,183,191). - The Summary column is required: if Summary/Strengths/Weaknesses is missing or empty, the output is invalid. - All extracted report content below must be represented in the final figure modules; missing or truncated modules are invalid outputs. - Do not alter any extracted factual text/value: keep wording, numbers, status labels, and signs exactly as provided. - In experiment tables, difference values annotated [GREEN]...[/GREEN] must be rendered in green text (RGB(86,133,44)); values annotated [RED]...[/RED] must be rendered in red text (RGB(200,29,49)). Strip the [GREEN]/[RED] annotation markers from the displayed text — show only the numeric value in color. [Rendering Guidance] - Make the figure as aesthetically balanced as possible. - Use adaptive typography, spacing, and box scaling automatically, but do not alter the fixed colors or the relative placement of modules. - Use clear visual hierarchy, concise labels, table-like alignment where needed, and publication-style spacing. - Match the original canvas composition literally: same dark header, same light body shell, same right-side stacked summary column, same lower experiments band. - This is a dynamic pipeline: for each run, first extract the teaser-display fields from the provided latest_extraction markdown, then compose the final teaser figure prompt from those extracted fields and the fixed style constraints above. - Only inject content that is meant to be displayed in the teaser figure; do not add extra extracted fields that are not part of the visible teaser modules. The cited location is §6.4; Table 3; Table 1 (WebNLG U columns). | ✓ Supported | §6.4; Table 3; Table 1 (WebNLG U columns) | [Summary] This paper introduces prefix-tuning, a parameter-efficient adaptation method for generation tasks that freezes pretrained LM weights and learns only a continuous prefix. The method is formulated for both autoregressive and encoder-decoder architectures, and evaluated on table-to-text and summarization. Reported results show strong parameter savings with competitive full-data performance on table-to-text, weaker full-data summarization results than full fine-tuning, and advantages in low-data and extrapolation settings. Strengths: - Clear problem framing: storage and modularity limitations of full fine-tuning for large LMs. - Method is concretely specified (objective, parameterization, architecture variants) with equations and implementation details. - Broad empirical coverage: multiple datasets, model backbones, low-data and extrapolation settings. - Strong parameter-efficiency evidence (e.g., 0.1% trainable parameters) with competitive table-to-text performance. - Includes intrinsic analyses (prefix length, embedding-only, infixing, initialization) to probe method behavior. Weaknesses: - Summarization full-data results underperform full fine-tuning (Table 2), limiting universality of gains. - Some explanatory claims (e.g., why preserving LM parameters aids extrapolation) are acknowledged as unresolved. - Ablation/analysis reporting is mostly qualitative in interpretation for certain mechanisms despite quantitative tables. - Main comparisons are concentrated on specific generation tasks; generalization to broader task families is asserted rather than extensively validated. [Experiments] Main result location: §6.1 Table-to-text Generation (Table 1); §6.2 Summarization (Table 2); §6.4 Extrapolation (Table 3 and Table 1 WebNLG unseen columns).
